title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery - Arclight Technologies
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38m
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Arclight CTO), Priya Kapoor (ML Eng), Sam Torres (DevOps)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick discovery focused on Redwood quickstart and PLG self-serve flow. Arclight wants to validate time-to-first-token, free credits, and evaluate whether hosted API is OK or if they need Dedicated/VPC because of data residency and latency SLOs. Agreed next steps: send quickstart guide, SOC 2 + KMS docs, propose short pilot with performance benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm maya from redwood, i run the quickstart motion, with ravi our solution eng.
[00:14] Jordan: hey thanks, jordan here. we have priya and sam as well, priya's on ML infra.
[00:22] Priya: hi, yeah. thanks.
[00:25] Maya: awesome, quick agenda — 10 min discovery on your stack and success criteria, then ravi can do a quick tech deep on the quickstart path, free credits, time to first token, and then we'll map next steps. sound good?
[00:35] Jordan: yep, good.
[00:38] Sam: works.
[00:40] Ravi: great, i'll try not to derp the demo, promise.

[01:05] Maya: first, tell us a bit about what you're trying to build and constraints. priya, maybe you start?
[01:12] Priya: sure. we're building in-app summarization and a support triage assistant that plugs into our existing ticketing. latency matters for user flows — tail latency under 400ms ideally for short chats; cost is also important at scale. we currently use an external api for some prototypes but paying a lot.
[01:37] Jordan: security is a blocker for some clients — they require SOC2 and want KMS + audit logs. some deals will require VPC or private deployment. not sure if that's needed for initial pilot.
[01:54] Maya: totally. that's common. for the PLG quickstart most folks start on hosted with free credits to validate functionality and perf, then we help scope Dedicated/VPC when contractual/security needs arise.

[02:10] Ravi: technical note — our hosted API supports streaming, function calling, embeddings, and you can pin model versions. for quickstart we give credits and a prebuilt SDK snippet; time-to-first-token for a basic request is often under 5 minutes from sign-up if you have code ready.
[02:30] Priya: under 5 minutes? what's included — do we need to provision infra or provide creds?
[02:36] Maya: no infra for hosted. sign up, exchange API key; we can give a sandbox key and credits. if you want to test latency from your region we can run a simple benchmark.
[02:50] Sam: we care about egress rules and IP allowlist — can we restrict inbound from Redwood?
[02:56] Ravi: yes, for Dedicated or VPC we do customer-managed networking. for hosted we support IP allowlisting per account and also SSO for team access. for strict egress or private peering you'd move to Dedicated or Private.

[03:20] Jordan: pricing — can you give a ballpark? we need to present to finance.
[03:25] Maya: i'll follow up with a pricing sheet. quickstart credits cover testing; for hosted usage it's usage-based per token and per embedding. Dedicated is committed monthly capacity. i'll send both flavors.

[04:05] Priya: on models — are you running open models or a mix? how does quantization factor in for cost?
[04:12] Ravi: we host vetted open models and provide performance/quantization profiles. we also recommend quantization for throughput-sensitive workloads. Opt-in by model variant — the runtime will pick kernels and quantized execution as appropriate. tacos.. sorry, takes a few commands to enable.
[04:32] Priya: (laughs) okay.

[05:00] Maya: what would success look like in 30 days?
[05:06] Jordan: demo a summarization flow integrated into our staging ticket UI, validate latency under 400ms for 95th pct, and validate security posture for pilot — SOC2 evidence, KMS for keys, and audit logs.
[05:20] Maya: great — those are actionable.

[05:45] Ravi: quickstart flow — step1: sign up with our PLG console, step2: get free sandbox credits, step3: run a sample request with our SDK or curl, step4: run a small perf script we provide, step5: optionally request a Dedicated eval.
[06:05] Priya: what does the perf script measure?
[06:09] Ravi: it hits batch sizes and sequence lengths you specify, measures p50/p95 latency, throughput, and token cost. we also provide KV/prefix cache suggestions.

[06:40] Sam: for network — do you offer private link / VPC peering?
[06:45] Maya: yes, Private mode supports VPC and on-prem options; Dedicated can do VPC peering depending on region. we'll need to scope network requirements and prod timelines.

[07:15] Jordan: if we start hosted, is there an escape hatch to Dedicated later without code changes?
[07:22] Ravi: should be minimal — same API surface, you can pin endpoints and model versions. rollout policies/route config are independent of infra. most customers swap to Dedicated with minor config changes.

[08:00] Priya: any compliance docs we can share now?
[08:04] Maya: yes — SOC2, privacy whitepaper, network diagrams and KMS integration docs. i'll send links.

[08:30] Jordan: ok, timeline — we'd like a pilot in the next 2–3 weeks if possible.
[08:36] Maya: doable. we'll provision credits today and share the quickstart repo.

[09:00] Ravi: i'll run through a short live sketch of the quickstart request (no slides).
[09:10] Ravi: (screen) sample curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"prompt":"summarize ticket: ...","max_tokens":128}' — response streams back the tokens.
[09:35] Priya: are you doing TLS client certs?
[09:39] Ravi: TLS for all traffic; mutual TLS is available on Private, not on hosted.

[10:05] Jordan: what's the typical p95 for hosted in us-west region with the medium model?
[10:12] Ravi: depends on sequence length and batching; for short chats ~256 tokens we're seeing p95 120-220ms on our optimized runtime in us-west on medium model — that excludes network hop. your tail will also depend on your client network.
[10:35] Sam: we have strict SLOs for one product line at 200ms p95 — that might push us to Dedicated?
[10:43] Ravi: yeah for strict sub-200 p95 at scale we usually size Dedicated and tune batching/kv cache; we can run a benchmark to show projected numbers.

[11:15] Priya: curious about cost — can you share a sample unit cost between hosted and dedicated?
[11:20] Maya: i'll include a sample TCO sheet. quick note: Dedicated lowers per-token costs but requires commit/seat. for PLG quickstart you're on hosted credits so you can validate before committing.

[12:00] Jordan: any limitations on model sizes? we might want 8k context.
[12:04] Ravi: we support up to 32k contexts on compatible models, runtime will select kernels. larger contexts affect latency/cost as you'd expect.

[12:35] Priya: does Redwood provide evals or regression monitoring?
[12:39] Maya: yes — Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. we can bake that into the pilot.

[13:10] Sam: onboarding — we have an internal provisioning process; who is the onboarding contact?
[13:15] Maya: i'll own initial onboarding, ravi will help with perf and integration. post-pilot, CSM will step in.

[13:40] Jordan: Ok, if we want to run a short pilot, what data controls exist — do you retain logs?
[13:47] Ravi: for hosted we have retention defaults but offer configurable logs/retention for Enterprise accounts. Dedicated and Private give tighter controls and can be configured to avoid persisting user data. we support KMS/HSM for key management.

[14:30] Priya: can we bring our own model later?
[14:33] Maya: Private deployments can support customer-provided models; hosted is Redwood-curated models. Some enterprise customers bring private model bundles to Private.

[15:00] Jordan: handshake — we'd like to run a two-week pilot focused on summarization, test p95 latency and cost.
[15:08] Maya: sounds good. we'll provision credits for the pilot and provide the perf script and sample prompts.

[15:40] Ravi: small demo note — streaming in our SDK surfaces tokens progressively and you can hook into UI. caching: prefix caching can shave a lot off repeated prompts.

[16:10] Priya: any blockers on our side? we need API keys, ip allowlist, and a perf collection script.
[16:17] Maya: we'll provide all three.

[16:45] Jordan: do you have references using dedicated for low-latency chat?

[16:50] Maya: yes, a few case studies; i'll share anonymized performance slides.

[17:05] Sam: how long does a Dedicated provision take?
[17:09] Ravi: depends on region and capacity, typical lead time is 2–6 weeks to stand up reserved pools, but you can start production testing on hosted while Dedicated is provisioned.

[17:40] Priya: okay — security checklist: SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, VPC peering. can you confirm those are available?
[17:50] Maya: yes to all; i'll attach the compliance pack.

[18:10] Jordan: what's the ideal success criteria to convert pilot to Dedicated?
[18:15] Maya: meeting your latency and cost goals and security signoff from your security team. we'll craft an acceptance criteria doc.

[18:50] Priya: what instrumentation do you expose for tracing?
[18:54] Ravi: per-request IDs, tracing hooks that integrate with opentelemetry and our per-route dashboards.

[19:20] Maya: ok, recap: we'll provision sandbox credits, send quickstart repo + sample perf script, send SOC2/KMS/whitepaper, and pricing + TCO.

[19:38] Jordan: great. what about benchmarking window — do we need to coordinate a specific time?
[19:44] Ravi: we'll run an initial bench from our side, then if you want to run from your infra we can schedule a 1-hour window.

[20:10] Priya: any gotchas?
[20:12] Ravi: watch out for cross-region network egress; also large batch sizes can increase latency spikes if not tuned. caching helps a lot.

[20:40] Sam: anything about data residency — do you have EU regions?
[20:44] Maya: yes EU regions available for hosted; Dedicated and Private let you pin region. we'll include region availability list.

[21:10] Jordan: sounds good. let's lock a pilot start date next week.

[21:18] Maya: i'll send a calendar invite for kickoff and provision the credits today.

[21:40] Priya: quick question — is there an SLA for hosted during pilot?
[21:44] Maya: hosted has best-effort during trial; commercial hosted customers can get SLA. Dedicated has SLA tiers.

[22:05] Jordan: ok we understand.

[22:30] Ravi: any legal/pricing red flags?
[22:33] Jordan: None yet; procurement will review if we move to Dedicated.

[23:00] Maya: next steps recap — i'll follow up with an email including links to quickstart repo, credits, SOC2, pricing, and an acceptance criteria doc. ravi will schedule a perf run.

[23:20] Priya: great, thanks.

[23:45] Sam: thanks everyone.

[24:00] Maya: closing notes — we often see time-to-first-token under 10 minutes for engineers; we'll try to make that happen for your team.

[24:20] Jordan: awesome, look forward to it.

[24:30] (some small crosstalk as people leave)
[37:50] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription artifacts — model names and network acronyms may be garbled, small filler words, and speaker attribution approximate.
next_steps: Provision sandbox credits and share quickstart repo - Maya
Send SOC2/KMS/compliance pack and pricing/TCO - Maya
Schedule 1-hour perf benchmark window with Priya and Ravi - Ravi
Share region availability and IP allowlist instructions - Maya

Maya Chen: Send SOC2, KMS, network diagrams, and pricing sheet by 2026-10-02
